seo.og_title: El Jadida Travel Guide | Cistern, Mazagan & Coast | MoroccoTripMap
seo.og_description: Portuguese heritage, ocean walls and beach time — a clear Atlantic stop between Casablanca and Essaouira.

hero_subtitle: Portuguese stone, a luminous cistern and the Atlantic — a UNESCO coastal city that still feels lived-in.

overview.title: A Portuguese city on the Moroccan Atlantic
overview.p1: El Jadida — historic Mazagan — is one of the clearest places to feel Portugal’s footprint on Morocco’s coast. The fortified old town, the underground cistern with its mirror of water and the ramparts facing the ocean make a compact, readable visit.
overview.p2: You do not need a full week here. Two or three days cover the UNESCO core, a beach session at Sidi Bouzid or the city shore, seafood and a calm evening on the walls. Casablanca is close enough for arrival; Essaouira or Safi can follow on a longer Atlantic loop.
overview.p3: Come for stone and light more than for nightlife. The cistern alone is worth the stop — and the rest of the old city rewards slow walking without the density of Fez or Marrakech.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: Cistern and walls first, beach and Sidi Bouzid second, soft third day for souks or a short coastal hop.

day1.title: Cistern & Portuguese city
day1.morning: Enter through the old gates and go straight to the Portuguese Cistern while light is soft. Walk the underground hall, then climb back to the ramparts.
day1.afternoon: Follow the walls to the Bastion de l’Ange and the Church of the Assumption. Keep a slow pace — the core is compact.
day1.evening: Seafood near the seafront or a simple dinner in town. Sunset from the walls if the wind allows.

day2.title: Beach & Sidi Bouzid
day2.morning: City beach or a short taxi to Sidi Bouzid for sand and swimming in season.
day2.afternoon: Lunch by the shore, then return for the medina souks and any rampart sections you skipped.
day2.evening: Quiet walk along the corniche; early night if you continue to Essaouira or Casablanca tomorrow.

day3.title: Harbor, photos & onward
day3.morning: Harbor light, Porte de la Mer and last photos in the fortified streets.
day3.afternoon: Travel toward Casablanca, Azemmour, Safi or Essaouira depending on your route.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting El Jadida

transport.title: Getting around
transport.desc: The Portuguese city is walkable. Use petits taxis for Sidi Bouzid and the bus or train station. From Casablanca, trains and shared taxis are common; agree taxi prices before long rides.

money.title: Tickets & timing
money.desc: The cistern has an entry fee and fixed hours — go earlier for softer light and fewer groups. Walls are mostly free to walk; respect private doors and military or closed sections.

dress.title: Wind & sun
dress.desc: Atlantic wind is real on the ramparts. Bring a layer even in summer evenings. For the beach, standard sun protection applies.

scams.title: Guides at the gate
scams.desc: You do not need a guide for the cistern or a basic wall loop. If someone insists, a firm polite no is enough. For deeper history, book a proper guide in advance.

safety.title: Swimming
safety.desc: Respect flags and local advice at city and Sidi Bouzid beaches. Currents can be stronger than they look.

q1.question: Is El Jadida worth a stop?
q1.answer: Yes if you like heritage and coast without a huge medina. The cistern and walls are the clear highlights.

q2.question: How many days?
q2.answer: One full day covers the core; two or three days add beach time and a slower pace.

q3.question: Best time to visit?
q3.answer: Spring and autumn for mild weather. Summer is fine for beach; winter is quieter and windier.

q4.question: How do I get from Casablanca?
q4.answer: Train or shared taxi are common. Journey time is roughly one hour depending on traffic and service.

q5.question: Combine with Essaouira?
q5.answer: Yes on an Atlantic route — El Jadida first from Casablanca, then continue south when you are ready.
